title: Signatures in Action: Code, Email, Web 🌐
description: From software updates to encrypted emails, see where digital signatures touch your daily life.

slides.title: Code Signing 🖥️
slides.content:
# When you download an executable (.exe, .dmg, .apk), the operating system checks its digital signature.

- The developer signs the software with their private key.
- A certificate chain links that key to a trusted CA.
- If valid, the OS shows the publisher’s name; otherwise, it warns you.

Code signing prevents malware from masquerading as legitimate software and ensures the code hasn’t been tampered with after signing.

slides.title: Email Signing (S/MIME & PGP) ✉️
slides.content:
# S/MIME (Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) and PGP/GPG sign emails.

- The sender’s email client signs the email body using the sender’s private key.
- The recipient’s client verifies the signature using the sender’s public key (from a certificate or keyserver).
- A valid signature proves the email really came from that sender and hasn’t been altered.

This is how organisations protect against phishing and email spoofing.

quizData.question: A valid digital signature on an email guarantees that no one else read the email contents.
quizData.explanation: False. The signature proves authenticity and integrity, not confidentiality. The email might still be sent in plaintext.

slides.title: SSL/TLS Server Authentication 🔒
slides.content:
# When you connect to `https://google.com`, your browser receives the server’s certificate.

The browser verifies the certificate chain and extracts the server’s public key. Then, during the TLS handshake, the server **signs** a piece of the handshake using its private key, proving it owns that certificate.

This prevents man‑in‑the‑middle attacks – a fake server cannot produce a valid signature for the real certificate’s public key.

slides.title: Document Signing & eIDAS 📜
slides.content:
# In the EU, the eIDAS regulation recognises qualified digital signatures as legally equivalent to handwritten signatures.

- Uses qualified certificates stored on secure devices (smart cards, HSMs).
- Guarantees the signer’s identity and the document’s integrity.
- Widely used in government, banking, and legal contracts.

Digital signatures are not just cryptographic toys – they are legally binding instruments.

slides.title: JWT & API Signing 🔐
slides.content: ## JSON Web Tokens can be signed with a private key (JWS). The API server verifies with the public key. This is a lightweight, stateless authentication mechanism that powers modern microservices.

quizData.question: Which of the following primarily relies on digital signatures for its security?
quizData.explanation: Code signing uses digital signatures to verify the integrity and origin of software.
